writeup.p: S34PacketMaps delivers a map item's data: VarInt map id, byte scale, a collection of Vec4b map decorations (type, x, y, rotation), a short patch width, a short patch height, and the patch bytes, each a 4-bit palette index into the map color table. MapData builds it from the dirty column region; a full refresh goes out every fifth tick, incremental patches in between.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleMaps looks up MapData by map id in the player's inventory, applies the column patch into the colors buffer, updates scale and decorations, and marks the map for re-render. MapData.func_176101_a (lines 244-246 in the bundled sources) constructs the packet; the 5-tick full refresh keeps the renderer honest when no patch traffic flows. The client trusts the patch dimensions and writes them into the render buffer directly.

None of the 8 clients has a module for this packet. The only non-vanilla hits are the Rise 6.x NetworkAPI script registration table (both 6.1.30 and 6.2.4) and the vanilla handler files. No ESP, no map exploit, no minimap integration consumes S34 in these corpora. Map pixels are world render data with no entity, inventory or movement signal, so cheat clients have nothing to gain from it.

The only theoretical abuse is server-side: a malicious server can send patch dimensions that exceed the map buffer and stress the client renderer. That is a denial-of-service vector against the client, not a cheat surface, and no client in the corpus defends against it. No anti-cheat measures S34 because it carries no gameplay-trust signal.

overview: Zero module hits in the 8 clients. Map pixel patches are pure render data; no ESP or map-exploit module consumes S34 in these corpora. The only non-vanilla reference is the Rise 6.x script API registration table.
server_handling: MapData.func_176101_a (lines 244-246) produces S34(mapId, scale, visible decorations, colors, minX, minY, width, height); a full refresh is emitted every fifth tick (field_176109_i % 5 == 0) and dirty-column patches in between. NetHandlerPlayClient.handleMaps resolves the MapData by id from the player's inventory, copies the patch into the colors array, refreshes scale and decorations, and triggers a re-render. The client applies the patch without validating dimensions.
protocol_notes: Wire: VarInt mapId, byte scale, VarInt icon count, then per icon a byte type, byte x, byte y, byte rotation, then short patch width, short patch height, then width x height bytes of 4-bit palette indexes. The patch is a dirty-column region; the full 128x128 refresh is a single patch with 16,384 bytes of indexes. PLAY state only, delivered to players who hold the map or stand near it.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat touches S34: it is render data delivered to map holders and nearby players. The only risk is a malicious server sending oversized patches to load the client renderer, a server-side attack with no client cheat counterpart.
general_hooks: No module hooks exist in the corpus. The packet reaches MapData exclusively through the vanilla handler.
client_variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 register S34 in NetworkAPI for scripts; the other six clients carry only the vanilla handler.
